text:
tara: Quick brain dump — I sketched a prefetch ownership sidecar idea to simplify prefix ownership + eviction boundaries. Wanted quick feedback before I turn it into an RFC.

mike: please paste the sketch. high-level tl;dr? :eyes:

tara: tl;dr: split ownership/lease bookkeeping into a separate process (sidecar) per node group. Runtime remains fast path for token-serving and local KV, sidecar handles: lease assignment, soft-evict coordination, prefetch admission, and ownership telemetry.

aleks: interesting. main win is smaller surface on the runtime thread for correctness?

tara: exactly. runtime only trusts an ownership token signed by sidecar. sidecar decides when to promote/demote prefixes and coordinates cross-node handoff. reduces distributed lease logic in runtime.

sasha: tradeoffs? added RPCs on hot path?

tara: not on the hot token path. runtime validates token (cheap). Prefetch decisions are async: runtime can ask sidecar for a prefetch hint; if sidecar slow, runtime falls back to existing conservative behavior.

mike: how do we keep correctness during handoff races? sounds like a new single-writer lease move.

tara: we keep the existing epoched lease concept, but sidecar is authoritative. Sequence: current owner sidecar issues a handoff intent -> target sidecar ACKs -> data plane continues to serve until final fence time -> sidecar emits a signed ownership token with epoch++. Runtime expects token >= local epoch otherwise reject write.

aleks: signed token = HMAC of (prefix, epoch, owner-id, expiry)? low CPU cost to verify.

tara: yep. example proto: ```
message OwnershipToken {
  string prefix = 1;
  uint64 epoch = 2;
  string owner_id = 3;
  uint64 expiry_unix = 4;
  bytes sig = 5;
}
```

sasha: eviction semantics? if sidecar demotes a prefix, how do we prevent races where runtime still serves stale cached KV?

tara: we add a soft-demote flag + grace window. When demote starts: sidecar marks prefix demoted and issues a demote-token with a grace-until timestamp. Runtimes seeing demote-token stop prefetching and begin TTL-based eviction, but continue to serve cached keys until grace ends. Final hard demote instructs runtime to drop cache and reject cached reads.

mike: sounds safe but relies on clocks (expiry, grace windows). we already do TTLs elsewhere. Are we comfortable?

tara: clocks are required today for leases too. Sidecar tokens carry expiry; runtimes enforce with monotonic checks and a small skew tolerance.

aleks: ops/rollback story? I'm worried about sidecar bugs taking down many nodes.

tara: good point. rollout plan:
- canary sidecar in a small region (10% nodes) w/ read-only prefetch hints enabled
- promote to owning for low-traffic prefixes only
- if regressions, ops can flip kill-switch to revert to legacy lease master (feature flag), sidecars gracefully emit a "passthru" token that runtimes accept as legacy.

sasha: what about observability? we need clear metrics: tokens-issued, handoff-latency, demote-count, stale-token-rejects, fallback-rate (runtime->legacy).

tara: agreed. proposal includes per-prefix histograms and a global handoff trace id propagated to runtime logs. Example query: `rate(sidecar_handoff_latency_ms_bucket[5m])`

mike: perf hit on verification? HMAC verify cost is tiny compared to kernel ops. we should avoid RSA here.

tara: HMAC-SHA256 is the plan, keys rotated via KMS and cached in sidecars and runtime.

aleks: multi-tenant concerns? can one tenant sidecar affect another's eviction?

tara: sidecars are sharded by shard-id which maps to a tenant-affinity set. We guarantee cross-tenant boundaries by not coalescing unrelated prefixes in the same sidecar shard. If we can't, fallback to runtime-only ownership.

sasha: is there any change required to the client API or model catalog?

tara: no API changes for customers. Internally models that require stricter isolation can opt out (private model buckets) and keep legacy ownership.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout checklist attached: https://redwood-internal/ops/sidecar-canary-checklist (link)

mike: one more: what's failure mode if sidecar loses state? e.g., split brain or crash mid-handoff.

tara: sidecar persists minimal durable state (current epoch per prefix) to local fast DB + replicates to peers. On crash, new sidecar reads durables, if missing it requests re-election via quorum. For split brain, runtimes check token sig+epoch and will reject conflicting tokens. We'll also instrument a safety alert when dual-owners observed.

aleks: ok. can we capture this as a post-RFC doc with sequence diagrams and the rollback playbook? I can volunteer to draw the diagrams.

tara: please do. I'll start an RFC draft and include a minimal implementation spike plan.

sasha: +1. add the canary metrics and the kill-switch steps in the playbook. Also add a concrete TTL skew tolerance (e.g., 250ms) so implementers have a number.

tara: noted. next actions:
- tara: draft RFC + diagrams (EOD Fri)
- aleks: write token proto and verification thin client (PR)
- mike: sketch canary checkout test harness and failure-injection plan
- sasha: ops rollback playbook and dashboards

mike: thanks. one-line: I like sidecar for reducing runtime complexity. :thumbsup:

sasha: :shipit:

ops-bot: reminder: please file impact assessment in the RFC template (security & perf sections).

tara: thanks all — I'll drop the RFC link when ready.
